terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. `node src/packing.ts` runs the packing code, and `npm run types` checks its types.

tasks.title: Tidy a ref of either kind
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `src/packing.ts`, `refLabel` takes a `Ref`: a number or text. For a number, it should give `'OK-'` and the number with zeros in front to make four digits: `977` gives `'OK-0977'`. For text, it should give the text without spaces at either end, in capitals: `' ok-1042 '` gives `'OK-1042'`. Rafe tells them apart by asking for a length, and the compiler refuses that. Check which kind `ref` is in a way the compiler understands, and leave the first line of the function as it is.

Check refuses `as` and a `!` after a value in your lines, and reads `refLabel` for its result type. It compiles calls of its own: refs of both kinds must compile, while true or false, or a label used as a number, must be refused. It calls `refLabel` with numbers and text of its own.
nextSteps: Run `npm run types` and read the two errors for the body: which member of `Ref` is in the way?
Replace Rafe's check with one that asks which type `ref` holds.
In each branch, write what that kind needs: the zeros for a number, the tidying for text.
hints: `Property 'length' does not exist on type 'number'` means the compiler cannot use `.length` to tell the kinds apart, because a number has no length at all.
`typeof ref` gives the word `'number'` or `'string'` while the code runs. An `if` that compares it with one of them narrows `ref` to that type inside its branch, and to the other after it.
`if (typeof ref === 'string') return ref.trim().toUpperCase()`, then for the number `String(ref).padStart(4, '0')` after `'OK-'`.

tasks.title: Count tins or a sampler
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, `lineCount` takes a `TinLine` or a `SamplerLine`, from the top of the file. It should give the number of things Bryn packs: the `tins` of a tin line, and the number of blends in the `samples` of a sampler. The compiler refuses Rafe's body. Check which shape the line has before reading from it, and leave the first line of the function as it is.

Check refuses `as` and a `!` after a value in your lines, and reads `lineCount` for its result type. It compiles calls of its own: a tin line and a sampler must compile, while a tin line without its tins, an empty object or a count used as text must be refused. It calls `lineCount` with lines of its own, an empty sampler among them.
nextSteps: Run `npm run types` and read the errors for the body.
Ask whether the line has a property only one of the two shapes has.
Read each property only in the branch where the compiler knows it is there.
hints: `Property 'samples' does not exist on type 'TinLine'` means you may not read `samples` until the compiler knows the line is a sampler. Reading it to find out is the step that is refused.
The `in` operator asks whether an object has a property, without reading it: `'name' in object`. The compiler narrows the union to the shapes that have it.
`if ('samples' in line) return line.samples.length`, and after it `return line.tins`.

tasks.title: Tell not counted from sold out
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, `shelfLine` takes the tins on a shelf: a number once Bryn has counted them, or `null` before. It should give `'Not counted'` for `null`, `'Sold out'` for `0`, and `'12 tins'` for `12`. The compiler refuses Rafe's body, and it gives `'Sold out'` for a shelf nobody counted. Make it give each of the three, and leave the first line of the function as it is.

Check refuses `as` and a `!` after a value in your lines, and reads `shelfLine` for its result type. It compiles calls of its own: a count and `null` must compile, while a count as text or `undefined` must be refused. It calls `shelfLine` with `null`, `0` and counts of its own.
nextSteps: Run `npm run types` and read the error for the comparison.
Decide what `null` should give, and check for it before the comparison.
Think about which check tells `null` from `0`.
Run both commands, and compare the three shelf lines with the comment.
hints: `'count' is possibly 'null'` means the comparison runs for a shelf nobody counted, and the compiler will not compare `null` with a number.
`if (!count)` is true for `null`, and also for `0`, which is a real count. A check with `===` asks for exactly one value.
`if (count === null) return 'Not counted'` before the comparison.

tasks.title: Write the delivery line whole
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, write a function called `deliveryLine`, with `export` in front, from the word `function` to its closing brace. It takes a `Delivery`, from the top of the file, and gives back text:

- post: `'Post to '` and the address
- locker: `'Locker '` and the locker number
- collect: `'Collect at the shop'`

Write its result type. Write it so that if a fourth kind is ever added to `Delivery`, the compiler refuses `deliveryLine` until it handles the new kind: the lesson shows two ways. Then take away the `//` in front of the lines at the end, to see it run.

Check refuses `as` and a `!` after a value in your lines, and reads `deliveryLine` for its result type. It compiles calls of its own: a delivery of each kind must compile, while a kind the shop does not have, a post delivery without its address or a line used as a number must be refused. Then it adds a fourth kind to `Delivery`, and your function must no longer compile. It calls `deliveryLine` with a delivery of each kind.
nextSteps: Write the first line: the name, a parameter of type `Delivery`, and the result type.
Branch on `kind`, and give back each kind's line from what that kind has.
Make sure nothing in the function catches every kind you did not name.
Take away the `//` in front of the last lines, and run both commands.
hints: Inside a branch for one kind, the compiler knows the delivery is that shape, so it lets you read the property only that shape has.
A `default` or a last `return` that gives back a line also catches a kind added later, without a word. With a `case` for every kind and no `default`, the result type does the checking.
`export function deliveryLine(delivery: Delivery): string {`, then `switch (delivery.kind) {` with `case 'post': return ...` for each of the three kinds, and no `default`.
